common.status: authored paper contract; not implementation or measured feasibility
common.scope: One deployed hero from three; three stages with a boss each; mid-stage acquisitions; identical world rules for manual and six-rule authored control.
common.observation_and_admission: At each declared observation boundary use current public fields; one pending request per movement/discrete channel replaces the prior pending request and expires at its next admission. Recheck its rule predicate before admission. A false predicate cancels the pending request; a false movement continuation emits STOP. Rejection is visible and requires a fresh command. Admitted actions finish unless their own cancel window permits interruption.

actions: ATTACK(named direction or declared target ID)
primitive_grammar.conditions: Each of six ordered rules can AND/OR named public predicates. No recursive call, search, auto-heal, auto-dodge or unspecified strategy macro. First true rule controls both channels; a channel not named in that rule emits STOP or clears an unadmitted discrete request. One action per channel; an optional paired movement+attack is stated explicitly.
primitive_grammar.route_primitive: Follow only the listed polyline at ordinary move speed. Advance the waypoint on its named arrival event; any explicitly listed waypoint wait is a fixed event gate, not a tactical decision. Stop on obstruction and show it. No detour, closest-safe-point computation or new route.
primitive_grammar.acquisition: Paused ranking is independent of the six tactical rules. Pause freezes world clocks, enemy/cast/debt/region clocks and recovery; selecting an offer or switching manual/auto does not reset them.

hazard_interface.owner: World hazard issuer, separate from special-mechanic owner.
hazard_interface.precedence: Already admitted movement, attack, cast and compulsory displacement are commitments. A new hazard cannot cancel, refund, rotate, teleport or shorten them. A later voluntary command may sacrifice a previously affordable escape and is attributed to that command.
hazard_interface.operation: Before a new lethal warning, inspect current recovery, declared command latency, existing walls, already committed hazards and compulsory effects. Try a finite authored list of candidate zone/time pairs in listed order. A pair is admitted only with at least one named authored escape segment whose ordinary traversal and projected committed motion stay outside lethal activation. If none qualifies, delay the new hazard and display 'no admissible warning'; do not alter an older commitment. This is a paper interface obligation; the reachability calculation and numerical bound are not implemented or passed.
hazard_interface.witness_limit: The encounters below state one available route and times as authored assumptions. They do not establish that arbitrary maps, latency, new combinations or all three heroes have a witness.
hazard_interface.pause: No hazard, expiry or compulsory effect advances while acquisition/stage-transition selection is paused; existing pending obligations remain.

candidates.title: Failed casts make an origin-sensitive exit obligation
candidates.relational_unit: Three actual cast interruptions fund one shared spatial jurisdiction: starting an eligible cast inside records a duty to cross outward before that cast closes. Moving into the region after starting outside does not create that duty; region expiry does not erase an existing duty.
candidates.abstraction_level: policy/rule; composed into encounter workflow through public cast events and authored movement

rules.mark_funding: A living equipped hero has three run-owned residue credits, capacity three. An admitted eligible ArcBolt costs five mana whether it completes or fails. A genuine pre-completion interruption (enemy interruption or admitted player CANCEL after the 0.5-second windup) with a residue credit and no active region consumes one credit and records (cast ID, center position, event ID). One mark per cast. Losing HP without interrupting, a rejected cast or cancelling before admission creates no mark. No XP/reward from failed casts.
rules.mark_identity_geometry: Marks are phase-owned and ordered by interruption event ID. Three distinct cast IDs consume all three marks. If triangle area is at least 0.5 square units they create one closed triangle for eight seconds; if degenerate/collinear they create no region, retain no marks and refund no credits. Boundary is inside. Feedback previews the three named preparation points and rejects neither real failure nor its cost.
rules.region_capacity: At most one region. Interruptions while it is active do not spend residue credits or create another region. On phase exit, remove unused marks and the region; spent credits remain spent. Equipment removal occurs only at paused selection and does not discharge a cast obligation.
rules.cast_origin: At admission freeze eligible spell's cast ID, owner, origin membership and region ID. ArcBolt and the disclosed enemy MireBolt have a 0.5-second immobile windup and 1.5-second movable recovery/commitment; their effect resolves at the two-second close. Starting outside grants ordinary completion even if the caster enters later. Starting inside requires an actual continuous movement crossing from inside/boundary to strictly outside after admission and at or before close. A mere command or teleport to a node is not a crossing.
rules.cast_completion: Movement and crossing events resolve before the same-boundary close verdict. If the recorded origin obligation has been satisfied and caster survives without cast interruption, effect resolves once; otherwise it fizzles once. The effect is not applied early. Current region membership alone is never the verdict.
rules.interruption: An interrupted cast closes without its effect and can fund exactly one eligible mark. A cast ID closed by interruption cannot later complete, cross successfully or fund another mark. Ordinary melee and movement do not require an exit.
rules.expiry: Remove the region before admitting new casts at its exact eight-second boundary. Existing cast obligations remain owned by their cast until its original two-second close, interruption or caster death; expiry never grants automatic completion.
rules.death_owner_exit: Resolve damage/hazards and caster death before a close payoff. Death closes the cast without effect or refund. Boss phase exit removes region/unused marks but preserves an already admitted living hero cast until close; a removed enemy owner cancels its cast without effect. Stage handover waits for a live admitted hero cast to close; no escape via menu.
rules.resource: Residue credits initialize once per run at three only when the optional tool is selected at run setup; otherwise zero until acquired. A later acquired tool gives no automatic free credits. An explicit residue bundle offers +3 capped at three at paused acquisition and replaces another offer; mana obeys inherited finite ordinary economy. Carry remaining credits across all stages; no phase refill.

expire region and close ownerless casts
admit new casts using current region
resolve surviving cast close once, then effect and its ordinary consequences

At each preparation node, the fixed waypoint wait is its one interruption-mark event before advancing; at H after the region forms, wait for ArcBolt admission then follow H→X; at M wait for ordinary route arrival before looping. EXIT is H→X. ESCAPE is the separately authored west corridor. All coordinates/times are witness assumptions, not prescribed universal level geometry.

Unsafe abandonment stops PREP_LOOP at its current point; no fabricated marks or automatic restart. Declared target is boss ID or a fixed named caster, never the most useful target selected by an optimizer.

stage_boss_no_tool_no_refill_recompositi.stage2: Marsh's mobile caster has a published exit segment and poison/add pressure. Preparing the region can cost its benefit; choose ordinary outside casting and cleanse. No compulsory acquisition.

authored_encounter_trace: Assume no lethal warning during the preparation witness, ordinary speed four units/second, sufficient mana at least twenty and the three shown nodes accessible.

At P1 admit ArcBolt, finish windup at 0.5, CANCEL legally: lose five mana, one credit, create mark a. Repeat at P2 and P3 with distinct cast IDs: three actual lost casts form the triangle for eight seconds.

At H admit another ArcBolt inside. After its 0.5 windup follow H→X; crossing x+y=4 occurs before its two-second close under the assumed speed. The origin flag remains inside while EXIT_CROSSED becomes true; effect completes at X.

A stationary enemy MireBolt admitted inside and failing to leave fizzles. An enemy starting outside then entering can still complete. If the hero's region expires midcast, its previously recorded exit duty persists.
Alternative: do not prepare; spend ordinary casts outside. This trace is authored arithmetic/event reasoning, not executed simulation or a success-rate result.
candidates.conventional_substitute: Compare a conventional anti-magic zone with an explicitly equal-duration movement-conditioned cast. Origin-latched obligations persisting past region expiry and outside-origin entry are the proposed relational distinctions. Neither global absence nor strategic advantage is established.

candidates.title: Withhold attacks to relocate a compulsory shove
candidates.relational_unit: One ordinary hostile hit loses HP immediately but its vector becomes a timed displacement debt. Moving without attacking chooses the debt's later origin; the next newly admitted attack or four-second timeout settles it once through current geometry.
candidates.abstraction_level: policy/rule with explicit action-admission and displacement interfaces

rules.arm: ARM_ANCHOR is a discrete idle-only action with a disclosed 0.2-second recovery. It consumes one run-owned anchor charge immediately and arms the next eligible hostile direct-knockback hit for two seconds. No refund if it expires unused. Capacity two, start two if tool selected at setup; optional +1 cache refill capped at two.
rules.eligible_hit: Qualifying accepted hostile direct hit resolves its HP damage, guard and death normally. If living, armed and debt slot empty, its post-resistance displacement vector is recorded once by hit ID and the immediate displacement is deferred. Poison, terrain, self-hits and reflected secondary effects are ineligible. If it has no surviving vector, the arm remains until expiry rather than inventing a shove.
rules.debt: Store vector, source/hit ID and exact four-second deadline from hit. Remove armed state. Movement and guard retain debt. Debt belongs to the living hero, not the enemy; source death and boss phase changes do not cancel it.
rules.second_hit: While debt exists, further hits cause ordinary damage and ordinary displacement; they are not merged, replaced or deferred. An anchor-arm request with debt occupied is rejected before cost. New hit can kill or change the origin at which old debt will settle.
rules.attack_release: A newly admitted basic or skill attack after debt creation requests settlement before that new attack's strike. An earlier already admitted attack continuing after the hit is not a new admission and does not retroactively release debt. Basic ATTACK(NORTH) is a legal free-aim jab at empty terrain at ordinary stamina/recovery cost, so release does not require an available enemy.
rules.once_owner: Debt owner marks the debt terminal before emitting one ordinary displacement. If timeout and new attack admission coincide, timeout is the recorded cause and the attack emits no second settlement. Interruption after attack admission cannot restore/reapply settled debt.
rules.collision: Apply the frozen vector from current hero center with ordinary collision, knockback resistance already applied at capture, and no second resistance multiplication. Walls can truncate displacement; there is no restitution, wall-generated refund or teleport. Public preview is current collision projection only, not a promise about future wall states.
rules.death: Incoming damage/hazards and hero death at a boundary retire the debt without moving or resurrecting the dead hero. Resource remains spent. If alive, same-boundary timeout resolves before another ordinary incoming displacement.
rules.stage_exit: Boss phase transitions retain debt and its clock. Stage-end handover/acquisition cannot discharge it: acquisition freezes the timer; leaving the stage waits for settlement/expiry while ordinary world consequences remain. If the hero owner is removed by run death, retire once without refund.

new damage/hazard effects from settlement follow ordinary world order; then feedback

authored_encounter_trace: Assume sufficient HP/stamina, north vector length four, hit at A, no new lethal hazard during the route, wall y=3 still exists.
ARM consumes one charge. The disclosed direct hit within two seconds causes its normal HP loss; store north vector and four-second deadline rather than moving immediately.
Rule 4 suppresses offense and follows the 0.75-second west segment to B. A later ordinary second hit would still displace normally; the witness does not assume it is cancelled.
At B a new admitted jab triggers one settlement before its strike: north movement stops at wall y=3 under ordinary collision. The debt is terminal; attack recovery is ordinary.

If the wall breaks before release, the unchanged vector may land in danger. If a pending attack is rejected it does not settle. If timeout and a jab coincide, timeout owns one release. These are authored branches, not executed tests.

Compare immediate knockback and ordinary knockback immunity with equal costs; no global first inferred.

candidates.title: Amend public gate law after the enemy acquires its route
candidates.relational_unit: The gate acts on the current public source clause, while a scout carries one publicly acquired older clause as a committed finite route. Editing changes world truth immediately and changes the scout's next plan only at its next inspection.
candidates.abstraction_level: policy/rule and versioned observation interface; not unrestricted rule programming

rules.map: One physical placard P, marked tiles EAST and NORTH, ward gate WEST and two fixed route tables are authored. The flyer can bypass ordinary walls but cannot bypass the gate's disclosed ward. Hero and scout crossing the current source tile have identical trigger rights.
rules.law: Initial law version v0 says outside→inside crossing of EAST opens WEST for 1.5 seconds. AMEND(NORTH) is an idle-only placard interaction within its named radius: 0.4-second admitted operation, consume one amendment at admission, change source and increment version at completion. Cost remains after interruption; failed operation makes no change. One amendment allowed per phase; no free reversal. Current law is public continuously.
rules.source_crossing: Trigger only a genuine outside→inside center crossing of the current source tile, not standing, a requested path, exiting the tile or an old acquired clause. Refresh one gate interval to max(current close, crossing time+1.5), no stacked tokens. Process by stable event ID.
rules.gate: WEST crossing admission tests current open interval with strict time < close. An already admitted gate passage takes 0.5 seconds and completes normally even if gate closes; closure rejects later arrivals and does not crush, teleport or eject occupants. Open-to-closed interval is public. Standing at a closed entrance does not pass.
rules.scout_inspection: At P, READ lasts 0.5 seconds. At its completion copy current law/version and select exactly the table for that source: EAST→WEST→RETURN or NORTH→WEST→RETURN. Show source, read version and finite route. Commit for at most six seconds; no replan on a law edit.
rules.route_commit: Scout follows acquired route and its fixed waypoint timing at ordinary disclosed speed. A closed WEST rejects passage visibly; scout waits at its gate entrance until opening or six-second commitment deadline. At deadline abort remaining route and follow a fixed two-second RETURN path to P, then READ again. It may not choose a new source midway. Death/owner exit retires route once.
rules.public_edit_window: For the paper fixture READ completes at t0; source crossing is scheduled t0+2 and WEST arrival t0+2.5 if geometry permits. Placard is reachable by the hero at t0+0.6 and amendment can complete at t0+1.0. These are authored fixture assumptions. An obstructed source segment may make arrival later; the public countdown updates physical progress without changing the acquired route.
rules.combat: Scout retains one disclosed ordinary attack opportunity per commitment at its fixed waypoint. Blocking its gate route does not damage or defeat it automatically; it can be killed normally, and a boss retains ordinary recovery/HP defeat. No unlimited attack/XP generation from repeated failed routes.
rules.resource_owner_exit: Amendments run-owned, capacity two, start two with optional setup tool; optional +1 cache refill capped at two; no automatic phase refill. Phase owns law/gate/scout commitments and initializes EAST once on entry. Owner exit cancels unfinished reads/routes and closes the removed gate; spent amendments persist. Stage transition waits for living hero's admitted amendment recovery to end.
rules.pause: Paused acquisition freezes read/edit/route/gate clocks; changes in command source do not reset a read version, grant an inspection or discharge a queued crossing.

authored_encounter_trace: Assume READ completes at t0 with EAST/v0; scout route shows EAST crossing at +2, WEST arrival +2.5 and commitment limit +6.
Hero's fixed ACCESS reaches P at +0.6; AMEND completes at +1, spending a charge and setting NORTH/v1. Scout publicly retains EAST/v0.

At +2 scout crosses EAST: no current-law trigger. At +2.5 WEST is closed and passage rejects. Scout waits without changing source until +6, then returns in its fixed two-second route and reads NORTH/v1.
Counterbranch: hero or another enemy crosses NORTH at +2.1; WEST opens until +3.6, so the scout's still-stale route can pass at +2.5. Staleness is not immunity to current world events.
Without amendment EAST opens WEST normally. At exact same boundary completed edit precedes tile crossing and READ: both evaluate the new law. These are authored branches, not observed AI behavior.
